A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoMeco/MIRA study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–F support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six meta-cognition lenses and MIRA across three LLMs and three mathematical datasets, with additional correlations and case studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds PRM-based voting results, latency measurements, and agreement measurements between two PRM judges.

M1.justification: AutoMeco's annotation and evaluation pipeline and MIRA's backward Q-value propagation and normalization remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedure; the additional PRM supports an agreement analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH500, and MinervaMATH with the same mathematical reasoning coverage. The added timing and judge-agreement experiments use retained datasets and reasoning traces.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds PRM-based voting alongside majority voting across all three models and datasets. The six existing lenses and their MIRA variants are retained. Skywork is additionally evaluated as a second annotation judge in Section 4.4.

E3.justification: New protocols measure per-step and per-instance latency on Qwen2.5-7B/GSM8K and compare PRMs using step-level and step-averaged instance rewards. Table 4 introduces Pearson correlation and Cohen's kappa, maximizing kappa over binarization thresholds from 0.1 to 0.9. Existing generation and Best-of-N settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds two targeted analyses: MIRA's computational overhead and agreement between Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B and Skywork-o1-Open-PRM-Qwen-2.5-7B. The existing AutoMeco–Best-of-N consistency analysis, lens ablations, appendix correlations, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The new inter-PRM analysis adds Pearson correlation and Cohen's kappa estimation, reporting correlation significance at p < 0.05 in Table 4. Existing rank-correlation p-values are unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or variability estimates are added.

E6.justification: New results include PRM-voting accuracy of 13.97% for Qwen2.5-7B on MinervaMATH, CoE-C latency of 3.31 ms without versus 3.34 ms with MIRA, and Qwen-trace PRM kappa of 0.3274 at step level versus 0.5878 at instance level. Existing lens/MIRA scores, consistency results, appendix tables, and case-study values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 removes a duplicated Q-value equation: v1 Equations 9–11 become v2 Equations 9–10 while retaining both the expected-value expression and deterministic simplification. This does not change the mathematical reasoning. Appendix definitions and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about AutoMeco's automated benchmarking and MIRA's training-free improvement of meta-cognition lenses. The additional experiments support those existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the timing results as negligible MIRA overhead and the cross-PRM results as supporting judge reliability, while acknowledging weaker step-level agreement. A new limitations paragraph explicitly discusses restrictions imposed by access to model internals, especially for hidden-state methods on closed models.

D1.justification: v1 promises code upon publication; v2 supplies an explicit AutoMeco repository link. This improves documented access information without establishing external availability. Existing hardware, generation settings, and Appendix C prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Skywork (He et al.), GPT-4 (Achiam et al.), Pearson correlation, and kappa reliability (McHugh). These support the added analysis and limitation; Section 2's research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits streamline the Q-value exposition, expand experimental discussion and subheadings, add acknowledgments, and update author contact and equal-contribution information. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds latency and PRM-agreement tables, expands Table 2's baseline row and caption, and updates Figure 1 terminology and Figure 3's caption. Appendix tables and prompt boxes are reformatted or relocated; existing plots and case-study figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The PRM baseline, latency measurements, and second-judge analysis provide useful additional context for the unchanged core results. Explicit model-access limitations and code access information also improve transparency. The gains are limited: threshold-optimized agreement between automated judges does not establish annotation accuracy against human judgments, and step-level agreement remains weaker than instance-level agreement.
